title: Sanitation Infrastructure and Environmental Vulnerability of Hepatitis A Transmission in South Korea, 2020-2024: Nationwide Bayesian Hierarchical Analysis (analysis code and compiled data, v2.0.5)
description: Corrected, submission-aligned reproducibility package for a Bayesian spatiotemporal analysis of district-level hepatitis A incidence across 223 South Korean districts, 2020-2024 (negative binomial, Besag-York-Mollie convolution + RW1 + Knorr-Held Type I interaction, fitted with R-INLA). Contains the R script for the final 27-covariate model, the compiled 1,112-row district-year analytic dataset, principal-model incidence-rate ratios, model-comparison and spatial-residual diagnostics, CPO/PIT values, a VIF audit, run logs and R/INLA session information. The final covariate specification was developed exploratorily; the reported credible associations are hypothesis-generating. Supersedes v1.x, which carried the pre-correction script and no compiled data. v2.0.2 aligned the archive title and script header with the manuscript submitted to One Health (Elsevier); v2.0.3 aligned the covariate names in the README with manuscript Table 2 and corrects a script comment that described the swine/poultry specificity check as farm density rather than farm counts. v2.0.4 updates the title and target journal to the manuscript submitted to JMIR Public Health and Surveillance and re-labels the supplementary references as Multimedia Appendices. v2.0.5 is documentation-only: the two archived principal-model fits (core_run.log and core_diagnostics.csv) and the fit criteria reported in the manuscript are now listed side by side, matching the reproducibility disclosure in the submitted Methods.
